headline: Preprint reports that outcome-routed lessons can carry chance into later agent decisions
summary: A preprint submitted to arXiv on October 12, 2026, reports a registered synthetic study of whether model-written lessons can transmit random outcomes into later agent choices. Across 256 two-tool worlds, the authors report that after a more reliable tool failed by chance, readers shown its outcome-routed lesson chose the worse tool in 11.6% of next-run choices, compared with 0.4% with irrelevant memory and 0.4% with a success-written lesson. The reported panel interaction was +0.112 (95% interval +0.097 to +0.126) across 11 served model endpoints. The authors report that two writing-instruction variants reduced the panel effect but did not meet their harm-reduction rule at every affected endpoint. The study tests one stored lesson and one constrained synthetic choice; it does not measure deployed self-improvement, accumulated memory, or real-system prevalence, and it cannot separate lesson advice from a repeated failure report. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction.
